newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom, Satelindo in satellite talks.
newsitem.headline: Telkom, Satelindo in satellite talks.

text.p: Indonesia's largest telecommunications firm PT Telkom and joint-venture PT Satelindo are likely to jointly acquire and operate the new generation Palapa D satellite, company officials said on Wednesday.
"Both parties are still negotiating on the cooperation agreement but it is likely to be finalised by the end of this year," a Telkom official said.
He also said that President Suharto had given his approval for Telkom to launch the new satellite with Satelindo as a partner.
The new satellite is expected to replace the existing Palapa B2R communications satellite and is scheduled to be launched in 1998, the official said.
Satelindo is owned 25 percent by Deutsche Telekom unit DeteMobil and 22.5 percent by Telkom.
Shares in Telkom rose on Wednesday on market talk that Deutsche Telekom might buy a stake in the firm, brokers said.
Telkom was up 125 rupiah at 3,825 rupiah on a volume of 3.6 million shares by late afternoon after rising to 3,850 rupiah in early trade.
Currently, the president director of Telkom, Asman Akhir Nasution, is on an overseas roadshow to promote private placement, the company official said.
Telkom is also listed in New York and in London.
